# dsh-plugin-threejs-workbench — Three.js workbench for DeepSeek Harness
Two surfaces in the DSH Web UI, backed by one host route prefix (`/api/threejs`):

1. **A live preview of a scene file from the session's workspace.**
The header chip opens a slide-ov

er drawer (`shell.overlay`) with the project
report on the left and an iframe on the right. The ifra

me is served by the
host as a real page: an import map maps `three`, `three/webgpu`, `three/tsl`,
`t

hree/addons/` and `three/examples/jsm/` either onto the project's own
installed three or onto the co

py vendored with this plugin (three 0.186.1 —
`build/` plus the whole `examples/jsm/` tree, so `thre

e/addons/**` resolves
offline), a bootstrap module imports the chosen file and calls its exported
en

try point (`init` / `start` / `createScene` / `setup` / `main` / `default`),
and an error/console br

idge mirrors every page error, unhandled rejection and
`console.*` call into the drawer's console st

rip — the agent's code is
observable without leaving the harness. `.html` targets are served as-is w

ith
the bridge and the import map injected. Reload re-creates the frame; "Open in
tab" gives the sam

e page a normal browser tab (pointer lock, WebXR, gamepad
and fullscreen are allowed in the iframe).

2. **A project inspector.**
One scan per session (cached 20 s, re-run with Rescan) reports:
- the r

esolved three revision and where it came from (project install, a
hoisted ancestor install, or the b

three` APIs that newer revisions removed or renamed, as
`file:line:column` findings with the replace

ment, e.g. `outputEncoding`
(r152), `sRGBEncoding` (r152), `useLegacyLights` (gone by r186),
`WebGL1

Renderer` (r163), `THREE.Geometry` (r145), `three/examples/js/*`
(r148), `WebGPURenderer` addon path

s (r167), `RGBELoader` (r180),
`PCFSoftShadowMap` (r186), wrong `tsl/display/*` filenames, `PI2`,
`a

pplyGeometry`, `postprocessing` → `RenderPipeline`;
- GLB/GLTF/HDR/KTX2/DRACO asset weights, so a 90

MB model is visible before
it ships.
## Where the data comes from

The host half registers one prefix route on the shared web server. Every route
takes a session id an

d resolves the working directory from the host session
store (`ctx.sessions.get(id).header.cwd`) — t

he client never supplies a path
root, and an unknown session is a 400 rather than a fallback. Files

under that
root are served through a token-bound byte route (`/api/threejs/r/<token>/…`)
after a `re

alpath` containment check, so symlinks and `..` cannot walk out; the
three package roots (`~three/`,

`~addons/`) are checked against their own
directory. Files are streamed, never buffered, so a multi

-hundred-MB GLB is
served as-is. Nothing is written and nothing is executed on the host.

`cwd=<absolute dir>` is accepted as a fallback root for callers without a
session; it is the only ro
ute input not derived from the session store.
## Install

DSH Desktop: **Settings → Plugins → add plugin**, type the package name. From the
CLI: `dsh plugin -
-profile <your-profile> add <name>`, then restart the harness.

The browser check boots the plugin's own handler on a loopback port, points a
stub session at `test/

fixture`, and loads
`/api/threejs/preview?session=fixture-session&path=src/scene.js` in headless
Chr

ome (system Chrome or a Playwright headless shell). It passes when the bridge
reports `loaded scene.

js` / `calling export init()` and no error row appears —
i.e. three was loaded from the plugin bundl

e and the fixture scene initialized
with a real WebGL context.
## Limitations

- Only ES modules run. A `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.jsx` entry is reported and shown with a
"build it first" not

ice instead of being compiled; point the preview at the
built `.js` output.
- The inspector is a tex

t scan, not a type checker: findings are regex rules
from the official migration guide. A finding ca

n be a false positive when an
identifier merely shares a name with a removed API, and `three/addons/

tsl/display`
filename drift is only caught for the names known to have changed. The scan
skips this

plugin's own package directory, because the rule table in
`lib/index.js` contains the very API names

it looks for.
- The vendored three (0.186.1) is used whenever the project has no installed
copy; th

e report says so, and the drawer header shows which copy is live.
- Preview rendering depends on the

browser: software WebGL is slow, and a WebGPU
scene needs a WebGPU-capable browser (WebGPURenderer

falls back to WebGL 2 on
its own).
- The drawer is read-only: it cannot edit the scene, and it does

not hot-reload
on file writes — press Reload (the session's file edits are visible to the
next scan)

on file writes — press Reload (the session's file edits are visible to the
